doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Comparisons to Ella and being called 'the new Jane Monheit'
summary: Early comparisons to Ella Fitzgerald, and mixed feelings now that younger singers are compared to her.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Didn’t somebody early on — I don’t know if it was very early in your career — someone made some comparison to Ella Fitzgerald with you. And I thought that was so unfair. Like why do you take that off as a starting point.

Yeah it’s like come on, I’m 20. I mean she is my idol and was a very strong influence, but everybody has to compare everything to something else. Nothing new comes along without the press telling all the listeners, okay, it’s similar to this thing. So if you like that thing you’ll like this. If not, look elsewhere. I mean nobody just says okay here’s the new person check it out and decide for yourself. That’s just not what happens. I mean and there’s already, I mean when I first started out I was compared to everybody. And now I see in the press young singers being compared to me, which is funny. A singer, whose name I won’t mention, I saw in the press recently was referred to as, “The new Jane Monheit.” I’m like I’m still here. I’m only 32. I’m not going away. I don’t need a new
Well that’s sort of what I was wondering about.
Although it’s flattering in the same way. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
MR. Like with the generational things. I mean it’s not a generation, it’s what, a decade thing or something.

Well there is constant turnover in this business too. We’re always looking for the new hot thing. That doesn’t mean that the thing that came before goes away. I mean it really was kind of flattering that somebody said that. It was like, “Oh really — you guys noticed me enough that you can say that there’s a new me.”
Yes like you become a touchtone for something, yeah.
That’s actually really cool. Although at the same time I was just kind of a mixed feeling thing. It was like how do I feel about this. I’m not really sure right now.
